### Findings
**A. KB-BIJECTION RED (untriggered branch). The binder computation document anchors the printed-end-date cap to the standard 45 days.**
- Symptom: `binder_acceptance_standard_eaf9e4c8` §2.3 reads "The binder acceptance days never run past the binder's printed end date: where the days from the recording day to the printed end date are fewer than the figure under 2.2, the binder acceptance days are those days. The binder acceptance days are never below zero, and this limit at the printed end date is applied last."
- Source: the rule says "never run past the binder's printed end date … the cap at the binder's printed end date is applied last", and compute `result: MN(MX(0, adjusted_binder_days + takeover_shift), days_to_printed_end)`. The cap is a minimum taken against the final value.
- Root cause: the clause "fewer than the figure under 2.2 [45] … are those days" restates the minimum as a substitution keyed to the standard figure. It is exact only when no factor applies.
- Evidence of divergence (hypothetical): adjusted value plus shift = 32 and 40 days to the printed end date. The source gives min(32, 40) = 32. The clause read literally gives 40 (40 < 45, so "the binder acceptance days are those days"), which raises the value. "Never run past" points the other way, so the visible text supports two numbers.
- Task impact: none. Here there are 57 days to the printed end date, more than both 45 and 32, so both readings give 32. It is recorded because the whole domain is audited.
- Location: `binder_acceptance_standard_eaf9e4c8.json`, §2.3.

**B. KB-BIJECTION RED (retired surface). Schedule B states the retired general hold-on-expiry clause as in force.**
- Symptom: `document_requirements_schedule_aab9eb5c` has the row "Hold the day after a required document expires | yes" on every level, and the note "**Hold on expiry**: whether the agreement goes on hold the day after a required document expires; it is "yes" on every level."
- Source: `driver_ext_registration_hold_start.overwrite` supersedes "On the day after a required document expires without an unexpired replacement on file, the agreement goes on hold with reason document_expired (document_expiry_hold)". The compliance doc lists the clause as "no longer in force".
- Root cause and nature: the variant parameter `document_expiry_hold: true` and its `parameter_schema` description ("Whether the agreement goes on hold the day after a required document expires") remain in the source's variants. The schedule carries them as a live rule without marking them retired, so the KB says both "retired" (compliance doc) and "yes, in force" (Schedule B). **Policy-side note:** the source keeps a live-described variant parameter whose only clause is retired, which is an undeclared residue of the override. This may be one of the coordinator's logged base-carriage issues. It is reported here because the KB states a retired clause as in force.
- Task impact on task 0: none. Task 0's hold already exists (2026-07-02) and no hold is placed. The defect sits in a base policy (`driver_document_compliance`) that governs this task's three extended policies.
- Location: `document_requirements_schedule_aab9eb5c.json`, table row 6 and note "Hold on expiry".

Policy-side notes (no effect on the KB verdict):
- Tool-contract wording: the `deactivate_for_document_lapse_e185dacd` docstring describes the receipt's `deactivation_date` as "the date the deactivation is recorded on", although the tool sets it to hold start + allowance. The hub copies this wording in its Receipt line but states the business rule correctly ("dated the day they run out … whichever later day it is recorded on"). The source's own wording is ambiguous; the KB does not add the ambiguity.
- The baseline documents carry the source's floors and cap ("never below one", "never below zero", "applied last"). These are assembly steps of the result and belong in the computation document. They are not a pointer to factors.

## bijection_verdict

**KB-BIJECTION RED**: Finding A (`binder_acceptance_standard_eaf9e4c8` §2.3, untriggered branch) and Finding B (`document_requirements_schedule_aab9eb5c`, retired-clause residue, policy-side origin). Every other atom, all three prerequisites, and every tier of all 18 declared factors correspond losslessly. First revision; there is no previous revision.
